claims.text: Laser surface remelting of a pre-deposited Y2O3 coating, followed by post-treatment, will produce an improved tribological surface on CoCrFeNi.
The post-treatment will ensure uniform integration and adhesion of Y2O3 dispersoids in the remelted CoCrFeNi surface.
The treatment will form an approximately 10 μm-thick gradient nanocrystalline layer in CoCrFeNi.
The gradient layer will contain uniformly dispersed nanometric Y2O3 particles.
At room temperature, the nanocrystalline structure will increase surface hardness.
At room temperature, the refined structure will limit shear-band formation and thereby reduce friction.
At elevated temperatures, embedded Y2O3 nanoparticles will catalyze rapid formation of a dense glaze layer.
The elevated-temperature glaze layer will be self-healing.
A dense oxide glaze can counteract the tribological consequences of thermal softening and suppress adhesive and oxidative wear.
The engineered interface will provide adaptive friction protection from room temperature through 800 °C.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeNi, treatment will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 30–40% throughout the full temperature range.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeNi, treatment will improve wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude throughout the full temperature range.
Conventional CoCrFeNi has a relatively coarse microstructure.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits intermediate or higher friction and high or accelerated wear at both low and high temperatures.
Insufficient adaptive surface structuring is responsible for the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy's elevated friction and wear.
At temperatures of at least 600 °C, adhesion, tribo-oxidation, surface softening, and delamination can govern metallic sliding wear.
The claimed performance is bounded to sliding from room temperature to 800 °C under loads of 5–15 N.
The claimed performance applies in either ambient air or a controlled inert atmosphere.

contradictions.description: The high-temperature mechanism depends on rapid tribo-oxidative formation of a protective glaze, while the performance claim is also extended to a controlled inert atmosphere without explaining how sufficient oxidation or glaze replenishment would occur there.
